html:
The Aro Confederacy was a trading network of the Aro, an Igbo subgroup centred on the town of Arochukwu, in what is now south-eastern Nigeria, from about 1690 to 1902. The map labels it "Ato trading confederacy", a misspelling, in 1880 and 1900.

The Aro did not rule by conquest. Their power came from the oracle of Ibini Ukpabi at Arochukwu, which people across Igboland consulted to settle disputes, and from Aro trading settlements spread through the region. Those found guilty by the oracle were often sold, and the Aro became the main suppliers of captives to the coastal ports of Bonny and Calabar for the Atlantic slave trade. Hired fighters from allied towns protected their routes.

After the slave trade ended, the Aro traded in palm oil and other goods. Seeing them as a rival power, the British attacked in the Anglo-Aro War of 1901 and 1902 and destroyed the oracle.
